items.title: Running a prototype or pilot
items.source: Draft for review. Written by an AI assistant from general UK small-business knowledge, not from a cited document. Check every fact against current GOV.UK and regulator guidance, and have someone who does this work review it, before it is activated. Rules differ by country and change.
items.body: A prototype is an early version used to test an idea; a pilot is a small real trial of how it works in practice with real customers. Decide before you start what you want to learn and what result would count as success, for example how many people use it, complete it or pay. Keep it small, set a time limit, and record what happens. Use customers who will tell you the truth, not only friends. At the end, decide with the evidence: go ahead, change it, or stop. A pilot that proves nothing because nobody set a measure only delays the decision.
